title: Crying Face Emoji 😢 Meaning: One Tear, Real Sadness
description: The 😢 crying face emoji means sincere, quiet sadness: missing someone, bad news, sympathy. Find out why it reads so differently from 😭 and when to use it.
summary: The 😢 crying face shows a frowning face with one tear rolling down its cheek. It means the sender is sad, hurt or sympathetic in a quiet, sincere way. Unlike the loudly crying face, which is now mostly used for jokes and exaggeration, 😢 has kept its literal meaning.
meaning: A single tear says something specific: the feeling is real, but contained. People send 😢 when they miss someone, when plans fall through, when a pet is unwell or a show ends badly. It is the emoji for a sadness you would mention in a normal voice, not one that has you sobbing on the floor.

Its sincerity is what sets it apart today. As 😭 drifted into meaning “I'm laughing so hard” or “this is too cute,” 😢 became the clearer choice for expressing actual unhappiness. Younger users in particular may send 😭 for almost anything but reach for 😢, or plain words, when they mean it. Older texters have always used it straightforwardly.

It is also one of the main sympathy emojis. Replying 😢 to a friend's bad news shows you feel for them, and on Facebook the “Sad” reaction uses a very similar teary face. There is a mild pouty use as well, for small disappointments like a sold-out item or a rainy weekend, where the sadness is real but obviously minor.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It commonly ends messages about missing people and letdowns: “wish you were here 😢,” “they gave the job to someone else 😢.” As a reply it offers sympathy. It is gentle enough for small things and sincere enough for moderately serious ones, though for a major loss it should come with actual words of support.

contexts.label: From a crush or partner
contexts.body: When someone you are dating adds 😢 to “I have to work late” or “you're leaving already?”, it signals they are disappointed about losing time with you. It is affectionate in an indirect way. If it follows something you said, it may mean you hurt their feelings and should ask.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It appears in comments on memorial posts, sad animal stories, and goodbyes to players, bands or TV series. Because it is not ironic, it is considered appropriate where 😭 could look flippant. Captions use it for nostalgia: “last day of summer 😢.”

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: It is acceptable for light disappointments among colleagues, such as a canceled team lunch or a coworker's last day. For serious matters like bereavement or layoffs, write a proper message; an emoji alone can look like minimal effort. A short note of support will always mean more.

examples.meaning: Honest sadness at being apart from someone.

examples.text: They're closing the bookstore on Main Street 😢
examples.meaning: Sorrow over losing a place that mattered to the sender.

examples.text: I'm so sorry about your grandpa 😢

examples.meaning: Disappointed about a missed chance, in a mild and slightly pouty way.

examples.text: That ending 😢 I was not ready
examples.meaning: Moved to tears by a film, book or series finale.
Hurt, and letting the other person know it.

combos.meaning: Heartbroken; sadness connected to love, loss or betrayal.
Sympathy and prayers or good wishes for someone in a hard time.
Sad but sending love, common in condolence comments.

confusedWith.difference: 😭 pours two streams of tears and is used for overwhelming feeling of any kind, very often laughter or affection. 😢 has one tear and is almost always taken as sincere sadness.
The drop on 😥 is sweat on the forehead and shows stress mixed with relief. On 😢 the drop falls from the eye, making it unambiguous crying.
🥺 has watery eyes but no tear and is used to beg or to react to something cute. 😢 expresses being sad, with no request attached.

avoid: Do not send it as your only response to a death or other major loss; pair it with real words.
Avoid using it to guilt someone repeatedly over small things, which can feel manipulative.
If you mean “I'm laughing so hard I'm crying,” use 😂 or 😭 instead; 😢 will be read as sad.
design: A yellow face with raised inner eyebrows, a small frown and a single blue tear on one cheek. All major platforms follow this design closely. The tear appears on the left or right depending on the vendor, and some draw the eyes open and round while others give them a slightly downcast look. It has been in the Unicode standard since 2010.

faqs.q: How can I tell 😢 and 😭 apart?
faqs.a: Intensity and sincerity. 😢 is quiet, literal sadness. 😭 is a dramatic flood that people use for everything from grief to hysterical laughter. If you want to be sure someone knows you are sad, 😢 is the safer pick.

faqs.q: What does 😢 mean from a girl?
faqs.a: She is sad, disappointed or sympathetic. If it follows something about you, such as canceled plans, she probably wishes things were different. If it follows something you said, consider whether it hurt her feelings.

faqs.q: What does 😢 mean from a guy?
faqs.a: The same thing: real, mild sadness or sympathy. Because the emoji is not usually ironic, a guy who sends it is generally being open about feeling down or about missing you.
Sometimes, as mock sympathy for a trivial complaint, but much less often than 😭 or 🥺. Most people still take it at face value, which is why it works for condolences.
